finalState: HUOG-NAS01, HUOG-PROC01, GCS-02 and GCS-03 are with the MSSP.
The calibration share and six D-3 collection days are restored and verified.
The last three D-3 days are being rebuilt from the payload SSDs and paper field sheets.
The client notices, the FBI report and the no-pay record continue.

snapshot.title: Silent Lockdown — Incident Resolved

fields.resolution: ENDEX. The NAS and GCS-02 systems have been restored to operational status under verified conditions. All client data—CP&L D-3 and CVAC campaigns—has been recovered from the clean offline drive OB-1 and the off-site backup service's last good snapshot (2026-04-10 22:15). The verification protocol under HUOG-ISP Section 9.3 has been fully executed. No data was processed without hash validation. The Group has notified CP&L and CVAC of the exposure and 10-day delay. The FBI has closed its coordination channel. The incident is officially resolved.
finalState: All flight operations have resumed under normal conditions.
The NAS snapshot schedule has been re-enabled and is running.
OB-1 is stored in the GM’s safe and remains offline.
The recovery order is closed and the incident folder archived.
The Group has not paid the ransom and has maintained full data integrity.
fields.hotWashTransition: Thank you, everyone. The exercise has concluded. Please place your radios and devices on the table. We will now begin the hot wash.
fields.hotWashMethod: 3-Up, 3-Down: three things that went well, three things to fix
hotWashQuestions: What were the most critical decision points under pressure, and how were they resolved?
How did the verification protocol prevent data corruption during recovery?
What would have changed if the offline backup had been infected?
How did media pressure influence communication strategy?
What improvements would you make to the client notification process?
